findings.text: `Servex/agents/tools.js`'s `spawn_agent` parent-default change (the `parent: args.parent ?? ctx.caller ?? null` line, under the "FIXED 2026-10-07 (token-accounting, parent/child answer)" comment) is sitting uncommitted in the working tree right now — `git diff` shows it modified, not in any of the six `token-accounting:` commits. `plan.md` item 13 and `findings.md` both say this is "already fixed, this task," so the written record doesn't match the repo: this is exactly the "no loose uncommitted files" trap CLAUDE.md calls out, and the requirements asked for every fix to be committed with clear attribution. Commit it (or revert it if on reflection it's too big a behavior change for an "obvious fix" pass) before landing is trusted.

`review/diff.patch`, the file this review was told to read, is empty — whatever step was supposed to populate it with the task's diff didn't run. Not this task's doing, but worth a look so the next reviewer doesn't hit the same empty file.

The one shipped code fix is good: `Server/session-cost.mjs`'s `find_transcript()` case-sensitivity bug (lowercase-only match against an uppercase worktree folder name) is real, the before/after counts are independently checked (499/2101 → 11/2101 missing transcripts), and the fix itself is a correct one-line case-insensitive regex swap — committed cleanly in `ea4a7e6d`.

`reconcile.mjs`'s session 1 ("plain session") shows the ledger reading *higher* than the real transcript ($11.71 vs $4.47) — backwards from the other two sessions and from the whole task's "undercount" narrative. `findings.md`/`plan.md` flag this honestly as unresolved rather than hiding it (plan.md item 3), which is the right call, but it does mean deliverable 2's "plain session" number isn't trustworthy yet — picking the task's own still-running session as the reconciliation subject was a shaky choice (its transcript is a moving target while the script that reads it is still running), worth avoiding next time a reconciliation needs a "closed" session.

`findings.md` and `plan.md` are thorough and well-sourced (every number traces to a named script or file: `scratch-scan.mjs`, `context-measure.mjs`, `post-analysis.mjs`, `cheap-first-tradeoff.mjs`) and plan.md answers every one of the owner's six Phase-2 optimization asks with what data it needs — no simpler approach stands out; the depth matches what a "bulletproof accounting" ask actually requires.
